name: East Germany (German Democratic Republic)
summary: The communist state set up in the Soviet zone of Germany in 1949; it built the Berlin Wall (1961) to stop people leaving and joined West Germany in 1990 after peaceful protests.

location.value: Central Europe: eastern Germany, on the Baltic Sea.

terrain.value: The North European Plain in the north and uplands in the south, with the Baltic coast.

resources.value: Brown coal (lignite), potash and some uranium.

disasters.value: Heavy air and water pollution from lignite mining and chemical plants.

population.value: About 17 million at the start, falling to under 16.5 million by 1990 as people left.

urbanisation.value: East Berlin served as the capital; Leipzig was the centre of the 1989 protests.

disease.value: Basic health care was free and widely available, but air pollution was serious in industrial regions.

migration.value: About a quarter of East Germans left before the Berlin Wall was completed in 1961.

economicBase.value: A centrally planned, state-owned economy; exports included Praktica cameras and Trabant cars.

tradeRoutes.value: Trade mostly with the Soviet bloc through Comecon.

wealth.value: Richest Eastern Bloc country but behind West Germany.

moneyAndTax.value: The Ostmark, replaced by the West German Deutsche Mark in 1990.

inequality.value: The party elite had privileges, such as access to better housing and goods.

governmentType.value: A communist state dominated by the Socialist Unity Party (SED).

succession.value: Power lay with the SED leader; Erich Honecker replaced Walter Ulbricht in 1971 with Soviet backing.

institutions.value: The Stasi (Ministry of State Security), which read mail, tapped phones and used a vast network of informants.

stability.value: The 1953 uprising was put down with Soviet forces; about fifty people were killed and 10,000 jailed.

eliteConflict.value: Struggles within the ruling party, such as the removal of Walter Ulbricht in 1971.

armyAndTech.value: The National People’s Army, and large Soviet forces stationed on its soil.

majorWars.value: No wars; the state was part of the Warsaw Pact.

territoryChange.value: No changes between 1949 and the reunification of Germany in 1990.

alliancesRivals.value: Warsaw Pact (joined 1956); close relations with the Soviet Union.

inventions.value: Few notable inventions; East Germany was known for sport science and the Trabant car.

openness.value: A fortified border and the Berlin Wall (1961) stopped people leaving.

communicationTransport.value: Railways and Trabant cars; people often waited years to buy a car.

religion.value: The ruling communists promoted state atheism; church membership dropped sharply by 1989.

artsArchitecture.value: The Stalinallee boulevard in East Berlin, built to official socialist urban-design principles.

socialStructure.value: A workers’ state with full employment; the Stasi secret police monitored many citizens.

sharedIdentity.value: Weak; many people felt German first, and watched West German television.

dailyLife.value: Shortages of imported foods such as sugar and coffee until the 1960s.

peakPeriod.value: The 1970s under Erich Honecker, when living standards rose.

declineSignals.value: Growing dependence on West German loans; mass protests, starting in Leipzig, in 1989.

outcome.value: Joined the Federal Republic of Germany on 3 October 1990.

overallCertainty.value: Basic facts are well documented; some figures are estimates.
